title: Delta-driven batch/caching inspector for SLO-safe config rollouts
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Goal: Ship an automated 'inspector' service that evaluates delta-configs for batching and caching recommendations, scores rollout risk against latency and throughput SLOs, and enforces safe apply/rollback via circuit limiters and SLO-aware routing. This ticket implements the core detection & gating pipeline + short canary flow and the playbook hooks needed by Console/Optimize to display recommendations and take action.

Context: Optimize recommends batching/cache profiles to reduce token cost. Past experiments show 5–18% cost wins but with occasional P95 latency regressions when traffic mixes change. We need a deterministic way to: (1) score a proposed config delta for SLO risk, (2) run a safe canary/apply with cohort routing and limiters, (3) detect anomalies early and auto-rollback when thresholds are exceeded, and (4) surface evidence in the Console for operators.

Non-goals: Full autosuggestion UI and model quantization recommendations (handled by Optimize). This ticket focuses on runtime-side analysis, routing, and rollback automation.
acceptance_criteria: Inspector computes a per-delta risk score (0-100) using traffic-weighted latency deltas, throughput impact estimate, and historical cohort variance
Canary flow that applies config to a shadow + 1% live cohort with SLO-aware routing rules and circuit limiter in place
Automated rollback triggers: p95 latency increase > 10% OR error rate increase > 2x over baseline within 5-minute window -> rollback within 60s
End-to-end smoke tests (unit + staging) that inject synthetic latency and verify rollback path executes and logs a clear incident ticket link
Console shows the inspector report for any recommended config with risk score, top contributing metrics, and recommended apply window
tasks: Design risk-scoring heuristic: delta metrics, cohort variance, SE-based confidence intervals (PRD linked)
Implement inspector microservice (gRPC endpoint) that accepts config delta JSON and returns risk_score + recommended canary config
Wire SLO-aware routing: add traffic-split policy that routes cohort by user-segment + latency budget enforcement
Circuit limiter: implement soft and hard limits (soft = alert and throttle to 0.5x; hard = immediate revert), plumb to orchestrator
Anomaly detector: stream p50/p95/p999 latency, throughput, error rates; compute short-window z-score and sustained delta scoring
Integrate with Console: embed inspector report and one-click canary/apply/rollback buttons, include links to playbook
Build chaos/staging scenarios to validate: token-latency skew, KV cache cold-start, high-concurrency bursts
Add metrics & dashboards: Grafana panels for cohort latency deltas, risk_score timeline, rollback events
Create runbook: decision flow for manual overrides, escalation, and postmortem template
implementation_notes: Risk score inputs: baseline latency distribution, expected batch size change, KV cache hit-rate delta, upstream model variant latency profile
Prefer streaming anomaly detection using the existing telemetry pipeline (kafka -> streaming analyzer). Avoid polling where possible.
Use shadow traffic to verify functional compatibility but use tiny live cohorts for real SLO signal; start at 0.5% for high-risk configs
Circuit limiter should be configurable per-customer: allow stricter limits for Dedicated/Private deployments
Store all inspector evaluations in a compact audit log (immutable) for compliance and RCA
Expose 'explain' fields in the inspector response listing top 3 metric contributors to risk (e.g., "p95_increase: 12%", "kv_hit_drop: 6ppt")

next_steps: Stabilize risk scorer thresholds based on 2 weeks of historical traffic slices; metric owner: telemetry
Finalize default canary size and soft/hard limit values (Ops + SRE + PM decision)
Add rollback simulation tests and run on staging; verify no autoscaling thrash

postmortem_plan: If a rollout triggers an unintended SLO regression, produce a postmortem that includes: inspector evaluation used, canary cohort traffic, telemetry snapshots, and timeline of rollback
Record lessons learned and update inspector heuristic weighting; track regression frequency as a metric
